e-7053.knowledge_point: Computing the Integral of an Exponential Expression Using Integration by Parts Twice
e-7053.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={t}^{2}+1\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=2t, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}={e}^{2t+1}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t=\int {e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t=\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =({t}^{2}+1)(\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2})-\int (\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2})(2t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\int t\,{e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\displaystyle\int t\,e^{2t+1}\,\textrm{d}t.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=t\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=1 \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}={e}^{2t+1}\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t=\int {e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t=\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int t\,{e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =(t)(\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2})-\int (\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{2})(1)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{t\,{e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\int {e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{t\,{e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{4}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is a constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t & =\frac{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\int t\,{e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}}{2}-(\frac{t\,{e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{4}+D) \\  & =\frac{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}}{2}-\frac{t\,{e}^{2t+1}}{2}+\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{4}-D \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{4}(2{t}^{2}-2t+3)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C = -{D}.$ 

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t+1}\,\text{d}t & ={[\frac{{e}^{2t+1}}{4}(2{t}^{2}-2t+3)]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{{e}^{2(1)+1}}{4}(2(1)^{2}-2(1)+3))-(\frac{{e}^{2(0)+1}}{4}(2(0)^{2}-2(0)+3)) \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3}}{4}(2-2+3)-\frac{e}{4}(0-0+3) \\  & =\frac{3{e}^{3}}{4}-\frac{3e}{4} \\  & =\frac{3{e}^{3}-3e}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
